decision: Do not adopt blanket output relaxation. Test a declared parent-leg feedback relaxation while leaving learned leg corrections and both wheel actions direct, in one 64-update bounded block.
user_intent: Rapid coordinated leg/body braking, not minimizing leg motion or forcing smoothness.
positive_evidence: Leg-only intervention rescues low-friction yaw and low-speed retention without slowing wheel outputs; unchanged weights and reset samples.
limits: Low-friction linear braking still fails and some high-friction stops slow down; no 5000 admission, no deployment qualification. Parent-only relaxation differs from total-leg relaxation by 0.75 times the old learned leg residual, so initialized and trained functions must be compared explicitly.
